cards.text: My body tells me how I feel.
When I am calm, my heart beats slowly and my hands feel soft.
When I am upset, my heart can beat fast.
When I worry, my tummy can feel tight.
When I am cross, my face can feel hot.
Listening to my body helps me know what I need.

practice.prompt: Where do you feel big feelings?
practice.reply: Thank you for telling me. Noticing your body is a great first step.

chapters.title: Feelings Have Names
chapters.summary: Happy, sad, cross, scared and calm.

cards.text: Feelings have names.
Happy feels light and smiley.
Sad can feel heavy. Sometimes I cry.
Cross can feel hot and big.
Scared can make me want to hide.
All feelings are okay. Feelings come and go, like clouds.

practice.prompt: Which feeling do you have right now?
practice.reply: Thank you. It is good to know how you feel. Every feeling is okay.

chapters.title: My Calm-Down Tools
chapters.summary: Things that help me feel calm.

cards.text: When feelings get big, I can use my calm-down tools.
I can breathe slowly, in and out.
I can squeeze my hands tight, then let go.
I can hug my soft toy.
I can sit in a quiet place.
I can count slowly to ten.

practice.prompt: Press and hold the ball to squeeze. Let go to relax.
practice.reply: Squeeze and let go. Your hands feel softer now.

chapters.title: Too Loud, Too Bright
chapters.summary: What helps when it is too much.

cards.text: Some places are very loud or very bright.
Too much noise or light can feel like a lot.
It is okay to cover my ears or wear headphones.
I can wear a cap or sunglasses when it is bright.
I can ask to go somewhere quiet.
I can say: "It is too loud for me."

practice.prompt: What helps you when it is too much?
practice.reply: That is a good idea. You know what helps you.

cards.text: Sometimes plans change.
A change can feel surprising.
I can take a slow breath.
A grown-up can show me the new plan.
First and Then pictures help me know what happens next.
Changes can be okay. I can do it.

practice.prompt: Let's take three slow breaths together.
practice.reply: Slow breaths help. You did it.

cards.text: Everyone needs help sometimes.
I can say: "Help, please."
I can point or show a picture.
I can go to a grown-up I trust.
Grown-ups are happy to help me.

practice.prompt: Who can you ask for help?
practice.reply: Yes! They can help you. Asking for help is brave.

chapters.title: Waiting My Turn
chapters.summary: Things to do while I wait.

cards.text: Sometimes I have to wait.
Waiting can feel long.
While I wait, I can breathe, count or squeeze my hands.
I can look around and notice things.
My turn will come.

practice.prompt: Let's notice things while we wait. Tap a star for each one.

steps.label: Look for 5 things you can see
Listen for 4 things you can hear

practice.reply: Great noticing! Waiting went by a little faster.

chapters.title: Playing Together
chapters.summary: Saying hello, taking turns, taking breaks.

cards.text: Playing with others can be fun.
I can say hello or wave.
We can take turns. First you, then me.
If I need a break, I can say: "I need a break."
It is okay to play alone too.

practice.prompt: What do you like to play?
practice.reply: That sounds fun! You can share it with a friend if you like.
